newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Burundi says sanctions hurt civilians, peace process.
newsitem.headline: Burundi says sanctions hurt civilians, peace process.

text.p: Burundi's government on Sunday called for the lifting of economic sanctions imposed on it by neighbouring states to try to force military strongman Pierre Buyoya out of power.

External Affairs and Cooperation Minister Luc Rukingama told journalists the sanctions imposed on the small central African country were hurting the civilian population and hindering peace negotiations with opposition parties and Hutu rebels.

Burundi's neighbours slapped an economic blockade on Buyoya's government following a coup that ousted civilian Hutu President Sylvestre Ntibantunganya. However they have eased the sanctions in the last few months.
"Sanctions have been hitting mainly the ordinary people," said Rukingama, who is attending this week's summit of the Organisation of African Unity (OAU).
"What is more serious is that the economic blockade has impeded the peace process because when the population is not fed...you cannot go to them and talk about peace," he added.

Leaders of the 53-member OAU who meet in the Zimbabwean capital from Monday, are scheduled to discuss the Great Lakes crisis together with President Laurent Kabila, who overthrew former Zaire dictator Mobutu Sese Seko to establish the Democratic Republic of of Congo.
